findings.synopsis: The remote web server is affected by a path traversal vulnerability that can lead to remote code execution.
findings.solution: Upgrade to Apache version 2.4.51 or later.

exposure.label: Vulnerable service reached from the internet

indicators.text: IPS/IDS alerted 1 time(s) on traffic to this service and did not block it: Apache HTTP Server Path Traversal Vulnerability CVE-2021-41773(91694) (from 203.0.113.45), matching CVE-2021-41773. An alert shows an attempt, not that it succeeded.

10.10.1.10 opened 2 outbound connection(s) to 203.0.113.45 (port 443, 4444) after 203.0.113.45 connected to the vulnerable service. This is consistent with an exploit callback, but on its own it can also be legitimate traffic; confirm with IPS/threat logs, payload or application logs, or host evidence.
After the flagged inbound contact at 2026-10-16T03:12:00Z, 10.10.1.10 began connecting to 3 internal host(s) it had not talked to before, over RDP, SMB.
10.10.1.10 sent 59.1 MB to external address 203.0.113.45 after the flagged inbound contact at 2026-10-16T03:12:00Z.

Independent signals agree: the IPS/IDS alerted on traffic to this vulnerable service from 203.0.113.45, the same address the host then connected back to, and the host then showed exfil, new lateral, return connection. Treat this as likely exploitation and start incident response; host forensics is still needed to confirm a compromise.

rationale: Base severity: CVSS v3 9.8 (Critical).
